question.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

In addition, we've been given that

$$
∇f(x,y)=y{e}^{xy}\,i+(x{e}^{xy}+2y)\,j.
$$

First, we substitute $x=t+1$ and $y=t-1$ into $∇f(x,y)$ to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =(t-1){e}^{(t+1)(t-1)}\,i+((t+1){e}^{(t+1)(t-1)}+2(t-1))\,j \\  & =(t-1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}\,i+((t+1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+2t-2)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1)\,j \\  & =i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =((t-1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}\,i+((t+1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+2t-2)\,j)\cdot (i+j) \\  & =(t-1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}\cdot 1+((t+1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+2t-2)\cdot 1 \\  & =(t-1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+(t+1){e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+2t-2 \\  & =2t{e}^{{t}^{2}-1}+2t-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the above at $t=-1,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(-1))] & =2(-1){e}^{(-1)^{2}-1}+2(-1)-2 \\  & =-2-2-2 \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$
